English.user: I've tried hanging out with people before, but I always feel like I'm only there for convenience. When I have no money or say no, they disappear. Maybe something is wrong with me?
English.assistant: I'm really sorry you've been treated that way, and please know nothing is wrong with you. It hurts deeply when people only value you for what you can give them and disappear when you have nothing left to offer. How long have you been carrying this feeling, and has it made it hard for you to trust anyone?

English.user: It has affected me a lot. I lie awake overthinking at night, and I don't have money to pay a counsellor right now. I'm tired of having to help everyone just to keep them in my life. What should I do?
English.assistant: First, please don't worry about money—speaking with a MindBridge counsellor is completely free of charge. Realising you are exhausted from people-pleasing is an important step toward protecting your peace and setting boundaries. Would you like me to show you the available times to talk with one of our free counsellors?
